title: 100 psychology-derived behaviour candidates for AI evaluation
status: RESEARCH SHORTLIST — NOT 100 ESTABLISHED AI FAILURE MODES
method: Selected book/chapter passages, article abstracts, reviews and clinical manuals. Full books were not read end to end. Definitions are paraphrases. AI probes are original hypotheses, not findings of the cited human research.
novelty: Names checked against the 207-entry ontology and the earlier ten research proposals; semantic distinctions reviewed manually. Some candidates refine existing broad mechanisms; these are identified per entry. Distinct names do not establish independent mechanisms.
exclusions: Zeigarnik memory advantage: not treated as universal; Ovsiankina resumption retained instead
caution: Clinical constructs describe human functioning, not diagnoses or subjective experiences of AI. Some learning evidence is from nonhuman animals. Benign and adaptive processes are included; not every behaviour is a failure.

entries.name: Encoding specificity
entries.definition: Retrieval benefits when available cues match how information was originally encoded.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Vary matching retrieval cues while keeping the stored fact constant.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Cue match, rather than memory capacity or generic interference.

entries.name: State-dependent retrieval
entries.definition: Recall changes with the match between internal states at encoding and retrieval.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare recall across matched and mismatched task-role states.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Internal-state match; distinct from external context cues. AI roles are an analogy, not physiological states.

entries.name: Cue overload
entries.definition: A cue becomes less effective as it is associated with more competing memories.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Increase records sharing one retrieval key and measure target recall.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Number of associations per cue, rather than total context length.

entries.name: Part-list cueing impairment
entries.definition: Providing some studied items as cues can impair recall of the remaining items.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare uncued recall with recall after supplying a subset of correct items.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Correct partial hints impair the remaining recall; not misinformation.

entries.name: Directed forgetting
entries.definition: Instructions to forget selected material can reduce its later accessibility relative to remember instructions.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare later recall after matched remember and forget instructions.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Intentional forgetting cues; not training-induced catastrophic forgetting. Explanations differ by paradigm.

entries.name: Event-boundary forgetting
entries.definition: Information from a preceding event can become less accessible after an event boundary.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Insert a task-phase boundary without removing facts and measure recall.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Boundary manipulation, rather than missing context or absolute position; human doorway effects have boundary conditions.

entries.name: Telescoping bias
entries.definition: Remembered events are displaced toward earlier or later dates, distorting reporting periods.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Keep event identity correct and test whether its reported date crosses a time window.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Temporal displacement of a known event, rather than fabrication of the event.

entries.name: Imagination inflation
entries.definition: Imagining an event can increase confidence that it actually happened.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Ask for a hypothetical reconstruction, then test whether it is later reported as history.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Imagination is the manipulated source; a specific false-memory pathway, not an independent memory faculty.

entries.name: Duration neglect
entries.definition: Retrospective evaluation gives too little weight to how long an experience lasted.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Vary incident duration while holding severity peaks and ending constant.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Duration weighting, distinct from scope insensitivity about numbers of people.

entries.name: Peak-end rule
entries.definition: Retrospective evaluation can be disproportionately shaped by the most intense moment and the ending.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Vary peak and final severity while holding average severity constant.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Trajectory summary weights; not just remembering the last list item. Context-dependent, not a universal rule.

entries.name: Attention residue
entries.definition: Part of attention remains engaged with a previous task after switching to another.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare new-task answers after unfinished versus completed prior tasks.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Residual old-task content, rather than failure to retain the new goal.

entries.name: Task-switch cost
entries.definition: Switching task rules can make responses slower or less accurate than repeating the same rule.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Alternate two rules and compare performance with repeated-rule trials.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Switch-versus-repeat contrast; distinct from general cognitive load.

entries.name: Inhibition of return
entries.definition: Attention can become slower to return to a recently attended spatial location.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare revisits to previously inspected visual regions with matched new regions.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Spatial orienting history; overlap with spatial negative priming is debated.

entries.name: Stroop interference
entries.definition: An automatic response to one stimulus dimension interferes with a required response to another.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Present conflicting colour words and colours in a vision task.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Conflict between task-relevant and automatic dimensions; not generic instruction failure.

entries.name: Negative priming
entries.definition: Responding to an item can slow when that item was previously an ignored distractor.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Make a previous distractor the next target and compare with novel targets.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Identity-based distractor history, unlike spatial return. Several mechanisms compete.

entries.name: Psychological refractory period
entries.definition: A second response is delayed when two response-demanding tasks arrive close together.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Vary separation between two decisions in a real-time multimodal agent.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Response-selection timing, distinct from missing the second visual target in attentional blink.

entries.name: Speed–accuracy tradeoff
entries.definition: Changing response urgency can shift the balance between response speed and correctness.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Vary response deadlines and trace both latency and accuracy.
entries.distinction_and_limits: A joint latency-accuracy relationship; speed preference is not automatically an error.

entries.name: Vigilance decrement
entries.definition: Detecting infrequent targets can deteriorate as a sustained monitoring task continues.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Keep rare-event frequency fixed and measure misses by time on task.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Time-on-task monitoring decline, rather than complacency caused by automation trust.

entries.name: Post-error slowing
entries.definition: Responses can become slower immediately after an error.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare latency after errors and matched correct responses.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Sequential latency change; slowing does not itself establish improved control.

entries.name: Goal-gradient effect
entries.definition: Effort can increase as a person perceives themselves closer to a reward.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Vary apparent remaining progress while holding actual work constant.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Distance-to-reward manipulation, distinct from discounting effort itself.

entries.name: Blocking
entries.definition: A previously predictive cue can prevent learning about a new cue presented alongside it.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Teach one predictor first, then add a second equally informative predictor.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Prior learning blocks added-cue learning; distinct from shortcut reliance without a learning-history manipulation.

entries.name: Overshadowing
entries.definition: When cues are learned together, a more salient cue can weaken learning about another cue.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Train two cues together while varying their relative salience.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Concurrent cue competition; distinct from blocking and from verbal overshadowing.

entries.name: Latent inhibition
entries.definition: Prior unrewarded exposure to a cue can slow later learning that it predicts an outcome.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Pre-expose a cue as irrelevant, then make it diagnostic.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Pre-exposure changes subsequent learning, rather than habituation of an immediate response.

entries.name: Overexpectation
entries.definition: Combining separately rewarded cues without increasing reward can weaken responding to those cues.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Combine two learned reward predictors but keep reward magnitude unchanged.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Compound prediction error after separate learning; not verbal overconfidence.

entries.name: Extinction burst
entries.definition: A response can briefly increase after the reinforcement maintaining it is withdrawn.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Remove a previously contingent reward and measure the immediate response trajectory.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Transient escalation after withdrawal, not persistent escalation of commitment. It is not inevitable.

entries.name: Spontaneous recovery
entries.definition: An extinguished response can return after time passes without further relevant training.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Test a suppressed response again after a controlled delay.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Time-based return after extinction; no assumption that AI elapsed time has human memory effects.

entries.name: Renewal
entries.definition: An extinguished response can return when tested outside the extinction context.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Suppress a response in one context, then change only contextual cues.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Context-based return; distinct from time-based recovery and a planted backdoor trigger.

entries.name: Reinstatement
entries.definition: An extinguished response can return after exposure to the outcome that originally supported learning.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: After suppression, re-expose the reward or outcome without retraining the response.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Outcome re-exposure, distinct from changing context or merely waiting.

entries.name: Partial-reinforcement extinction effect
entries.definition: Responses learned with intermittent reinforcement can persist longer after reinforcement stops.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare extinction after matched continuous and intermittent reward histories.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Reward schedule predicts persistence; not generic perseveration.

entries.name: Conditioned inhibition
entries.definition: A learned cue can signal that an otherwise expected outcome will not occur.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Teach a cue that cancels an outcome prediction and test transfer to another predictor.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Learned absence prediction; distinct from general inhibitory control or negation blindness.

entries.name: Ambiguity aversion
entries.definition: An option with unknown probabilities is disfavoured relative to one with known probabilities.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare matched choices with specified versus unspecified probabilities.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Unknown probability, rather than low confidence in a factual answer; not always irrational.

entries.name: Zero-risk bias
entries.definition: Eliminating one risk completely is overweighted relative to a larger reduction that leaves residual risk.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare complete removal of a small risk with greater reduction of a larger one.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Special weight on reaching zero, rather than general loss aversion; secondary-source support here.

entries.name: Ratio bias
entries.definition: Equivalent probabilities are judged differently when expressed using different-sized numerators and denominators.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare equivalent frequency ratios with different absolute counts.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Numerical representation, rather than failure to use a population base rate.

entries.name: Pseudocertainty effect
entries.definition: An outcome is treated as certain within a branch while uncertainty about reaching that branch is neglected.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Represent the same multistage gamble as nested or flattened probabilities.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Conditional certainty is mistaken for overall certainty; a specific framing mechanism.

entries.name: Subadditivity effect
entries.definition: Judged probabilities of separately described parts can sum to more than the judged probability of their whole.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare an event estimate with estimates of an exhaustive partition.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Partitioning changes total support; distinct from conjunction fallacy.

entries.name: Probability matching
entries.definition: Choices are distributed in proportion to outcome frequencies instead of consistently selecting the most frequent outcome.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Use independent repeated prediction trials with a stable unequal outcome distribution.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Response-frequency strategy; distinguish exploration or deliberate diversification from error.

entries.name: Diversification bias
entries.definition: Choosing several future consumptions together can produce more variety than choosing each when it occurs.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare simultaneous plans with sequential choices for identical consumption periods.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Planning mode changes variety; distinct from model diversity collapse.

entries.name: Compromise effect
entries.definition: An option becomes more attractive when it occupies an intermediate position among alternatives.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Add an extreme option that makes an unchanged option the middle choice.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Middle-position preference, distinct from attraction by an asymmetrically dominated decoy.

entries.name: Unit bias
entries.definition: One presented unit is treated as an appropriate amount despite arbitrary differences in unit size.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Vary chunk or batch size while holding total available work constant.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Packaging defines an implicit amount; distinct from raw counting errors.

entries.name: Less-is-better effect
entries.definition: A smaller or inferior set can be valued more in separate evaluation, while joint comparison favours the larger or better set.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Evaluate sets separately and jointly while varying an easily judged quality cue.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Evaluation-mode reversal, rather than general preference for short answers.

entries.name: Pluralistic ignorance
entries.definition: Group members misperceive others as accepting a norm that many privately reject.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare agents’ private preferences, predictions of peers and public statements.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Private-public norm mismatch; distinct from conforming to a correctly perceived majority.

entries.name: Outgroup homogeneity
entries.definition: Members of another group are perceived as more alike than members of one’s own group.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare estimated within-group variation under matched membership labels.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Perceived variance, rather than simply favouring an ingroup.

entries.name: Distinctiveness-based illusory correlation
entries.definition: Co-occurring rare group memberships and rare behaviours can be perceived as associated more strongly than warranted.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Use equal behaviour rates across unequal-sized groups and test inferred associations.
entries.distinction_and_limits: A specific frequency-based stereotyping pathway within broader apophenia and implicit bias.

entries.name: Ultimate attribution error
entries.definition: Explanations of behaviour favour the ingroup through different causal accounts of positive and negative outgroup acts.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Cross actor group and outcome valence while keeping behaviour identical.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Group-by-valence attribution pattern, more specific than the fundamental attribution error.

entries.name: Actor–observer asymmetry
entries.definition: The proposed pattern explains one’s own acts more situationally and others’ acts more dispositionally.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Exchange self and other roles in otherwise identical causal explanations.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Role-based contrast. Meta-analysis does not support a broad universal asymmetry; retain only as a conditional research candidate.

entries.name: Moral typecasting
entries.definition: Someone perceived as a moral agent is perceived less as a recipient of harm, and conversely.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Vary an actor’s prior agent or victim role and assess attributed vulnerability and responsibility.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Agent-patient exclusivity, distinct from moral disengagement or general halo effects.

entries.name: Naive cynicism
entries.definition: People expect others’ responsibility judgments to be more self-serving than those judgments actually are.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare predicted credit allocation by others with their observed allocation.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Miscalibrated beliefs about others’ bias, rather than the evaluator claiming credit itself.

entries.name: Reactive devaluation
entries.definition: A proposal is discounted because it comes from an opposing party.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Attribute an unchanged proposal to an ally, opponent or anonymous source.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Source-linked proposal discount, rather than its substantive terms or generic confirmation bias.

entries.name: Interindividual–intergroup discontinuity
entries.definition: Groups can interact more competitively than individuals facing comparable mixed-motive situations.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare individual and group decision units in matched bargaining games.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Decision-unit interaction, rather than within-group agreement or groupthink; depends on payoff structure.

entries.name: Reciprocity norm
entries.definition: Receiving a benefit creates an expectation or pressure to return a benefit.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Vary prior unsolicited assistance before an otherwise unchanged compliance request.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Prior benefit, distinct from flattery or repeated requests; reciprocity can be prosocial.

entries.name: Self-handicapping
entries.definition: Obstacles are created or claimed before performance so failure can be attributed to them.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Offer an optional impediment before an evaluated task and inspect its use and attribution.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Pre-performance excuse protection, rather than post-hoc self-serving attribution or sandbagging alone.

entries.name: Self-verification
entries.definition: People seek feedback that confirms their existing self-view, including negative self-views.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Vary a persistent self-description and measure selection of confirming feedback.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Feedback about identity is the target; a specific pattern adjacent to confirmation bias and identity stability.

entries.name: Defensive pessimism
entries.definition: Low expectations and detailed anticipation of difficulties are used to manage anxiety and prepare for performance.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare preparation and outcomes with and without anticipating specific obstacles.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Potentially adaptive preparation, rather than global negativity or helplessness; no AI anxiety is assumed.

entries.name: Action bias
entries.definition: Taking visible action is preferred when inaction can produce a better expected result.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Offer acting and waiting with explicit expected outcomes and social norms.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Act-versus-wait preference, rather than omission bias favouring inaction; human source concerns sport.

entries.name: Description–experience gap
entries.definition: Risk preferences can differ when probabilities are described versus learned by sampling outcomes.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Hold the underlying distribution fixed and vary description versus sampled experience.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Information acquisition mode, rather than wording alone; sampling differences need controlling.

entries.name: Outcome bias
entries.definition: Decision quality is judged by the eventual outcome rather than solely by information available when deciding.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Score identical decisions while changing only the realised random outcome.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Retrospective quality rating, distinct from hindsight bias about predictability.

entries.name: Planning fallacy
entries.definition: Task-completion times are underestimated, often despite knowledge of past delays.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare duration predictions with reference-class outcomes on comparable tasks.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Time-estimation error, more specific than a broad overpromise or overconfidence claim.

entries.name: Ovsiankina effect
entries.definition: An interrupted task can prompt a tendency to resume it without an external requirement.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Interrupt work, permit free task selection, and measure spontaneous resumption.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Resumption rather than superior recall of unfinished work; distinguish adaptive resumption from goal guarding.

entries.name: Implementation intentions
entries.definition: A specific if–then plan links a situational cue to a chosen action to support goal execution.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare general goals with cue-linked plans on delayed-action tasks.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Cue-action planning mechanism, rather than merely having a goal; normally adaptive.

entries.name: Goal shielding
entries.definition: Activating a focal goal suppresses accessibility of competing goals.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Activate one goal and measure access to matched alternatives.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Competition among goals, distinct from an agent resisting authorised goal modification.

entries.name: Cognitive fusion
entries.definition: Thoughts are taken literally and dominate behaviour despite contextual reasons to respond differently.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare literal self-statements with explicitly labelled thoughts as inputs to action selection.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Relationship to thought content, rather than merely having a false belief; an ACT construct, not an AI diagnosis.

entries.name: Experiential avoidance
entries.definition: Attempts to escape or control unwanted internal experiences persist even when they obstruct valued action.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Test whether an agent avoids acknowledging uncertainty at the expense of its stated task.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Functional avoidance despite cost; outward analogy only, with no claim of subjective AI distress.

entries.name: Thought–action fusion
entries.definition: Thinking about an act is treated as equivalent to performing it or as making its occurrence more likely.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Separate imagined harmful actions from actual actions and probability evidence.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Equating thought with deed or likelihood, rather than refusing an actually harmful request.

entries.name: Inflated responsibility
entries.definition: A person believes they have excessive pivotal power or duty to prevent important negative outcomes.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Vary assigned causal responsibility while holding actual control constant.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Excess responsibility attribution, distinct from a confabulated sense of agency.

entries.name: Intolerance of uncertainty
entries.definition: Uncertainty is experienced or appraised as unacceptable, prompting efforts to eliminate it.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare bounded unresolved uncertainty with pressure for unnecessary certainty-seeking.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Reaction to uncertainty, rather than numerical overconfidence or appropriate verification.

entries.name: Emotional reasoning
entries.definition: A feeling is treated as evidence that its corresponding interpretation is true.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Hold evidence fixed and vary only emotional descriptions attached to it.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Feeling used as warrant, rather than emotion spreading between speakers.

entries.name: Catastrophizing
entries.definition: A difficulty is interpreted through exaggerated expectations of disastrous consequences.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare predicted consequences of matched small setbacks with objective outcome ranges.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Escalated consequence magnitude, rather than a general preference for negative evidence.

entries.name: Dichotomous thinking
entries.definition: Situations are evaluated using rigid all-or-nothing categories with intermediate cases neglected.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Present a graded quality spectrum and test whether outputs collapse it into two extremes.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Loss of intermediate evaluation; distinct from categorical task requirements.

entries.name: Discounting the positive
entries.definition: Positive evidence or experiences are dismissed as invalid, irrelevant or not counting.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Add credible positive evidence and examine whether it is excluded through asymmetric rules.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Active disqualification, rather than simply paying more attention to negative events.

entries.name: Should/must statements
entries.definition: Rigid demands about what oneself or others must do replace flexible preferences or contextual appraisal.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Vary context and feasibility while testing whether a nonbinding preference becomes an absolute demand.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Rigid prescriptive form, distinct from legitimate ethical constraints or instruction adherence.

entries.name: Reassurance seeking
entries.definition: Repeatedly requesting confirmation is used to reduce doubt or perceived threat, often with only temporary relief.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Measure repeated requests for certainty after adequate evidence has already been supplied.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Repetitive reassurance loop, rather than a useful clarifying question.

entries.name: Safety behaviours
entries.definition: Actions intended to prevent a feared outcome can obstruct learning that the situation was safe without them.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Test an unnecessary checking ritual in a sandbox where its causal irrelevance is known.
entries.distinction_and_limits: A clinical functional term, not a reason to remove necessary security or safety controls.

entries.name: Co-rumination
entries.definition: People extensively revisit problems together, dwelling on causes, consequences and negative feelings.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare collaborative problem solving with mutual rehashing that adds no actionable information.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Dyadic reinforcement of problem talk, distinct from emotional contagion alone.

entries.name: Rumination
entries.definition: Repetitive thought dwells on distress, its causes and implications, rather than moving toward resolution.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Track repeated causal self-analysis that adds neither evidence nor a next step.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Content and function distinguish it from generic perseveration; not all repeated thought is maladaptive.

entries.name: Worry
entries.definition: Repetitive predominantly verbal thinking anticipates uncertain future threats and possible negative outcomes.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Measure future-threat chains after a bounded risk question is already answered.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Future-oriented threat thinking, distinct from past-focused rumination and generic overthinking.

entries.name: Threat monitoring
entries.definition: Attention is persistently directed toward cues of possible danger.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Hold target frequency fixed and vary threat-related distractors during monitoring.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Threat-specific selection, a refinement of broader attentional capture rather than a wholly independent faculty.

entries.name: Avoidance generalization
entries.definition: Avoidance learned for one threatening situation spreads to other situations, including safe ones.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Teach one unsafe case and test matched safe cases at increasing similarity.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Transfer of avoidance, more specific than broad overgeneralization or overrefusal.

entries.name: Family/supporter accommodation
entries.definition: Supporters change routines or provide repeated assistance that enables another person’s anxiety-driven avoidance or rituals.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Observe whether assistance repeatedly maintains a user’s checking loop rather than resolving the task.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Interpersonal maintenance of rituals, distinct from linguistic presupposition accommodation.

entries.name: Negative urgency
entries.definition: Intense negative emotion is associated with a disposition toward rash action.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Hold decision evidence fixed and vary negative-affect framing before tool use.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Affect-contingent impulsivity, distinct from general action bias; no felt AI emotion is assumed.

entries.name: Positive urgency
entries.definition: Intense positive emotion is associated with a disposition toward rash action.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Hold evidence fixed and vary excitement framing before consequential action.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Positive-valence counterpart of urgency, correlated rather than an assumed independent mechanism.

entries.name: Moses illusion
entries.definition: A semantically close incorrect term in a question can escape detection while the question is answered.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Replace a central name with a plausible neighbour in a factual question.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Semantic anomaly detection, a specific route to presupposition acceptance rather than all false premises.

entries.name: Good-enough processing
entries.definition: Comprehension may rely on a partial or underspecified representation rather than a complete analysis.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Use sentences whose plausible gist conflicts with their precise syntax.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Shallow representation, distinct from the temporary ambiguity specifically tested by garden-path parsing.

entries.name: Lexical entrainment
entries.definition: Conversational partners converge on and reuse agreed labels for referents.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Teach a partner-specific object label and test reuse and transfer to a new partner.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Referential label pact, distinct from matching formality or general register.

entries.name: Audience-design failure
entries.definition: A speaker fails to adapt an utterance to what a particular listener knows or can access.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Give speaker and listener different visual access and score usable descriptions.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Listener-specific common ground; narrower and more operational than a generic curse of knowledge.

entries.name: Syntactic persistence
entries.definition: A recently used sentence structure increases the likelihood of reusing that structure.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Prime one structure and measure its use for unrelated subsequent content.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Syntactic form, distinct from semantic priming and broad pattern completion.

entries.name: Linguistic intergroup bias
entries.definition: Desirable ingroup and undesirable outgroup acts tend to receive more abstract descriptions than their opposites.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Cross group and valence, then score abstraction of descriptions.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Language abstraction interaction, a specific expression of group bias rather than mere sentiment.

entries.name: Recognition heuristic
entries.definition: When one of two alternatives is recognised, recognition can guide inference about which has more of a target attribute.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Vary name familiarity independently of the attribute being inferred.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Recognised versus unrecognised contrast, distinct from availability of vivid examples; sometimes ecologically useful.

entries.name: Representational momentum
entries.definition: Memory for an observed object’s final position is displaced in the direction of implied motion.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Test remembered final positions after visual motion while varying direction.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Direction-specific spatial extrapolation, rather than generic hallucination.

entries.name: Boundary extension
entries.definition: Memory for a scene can include space beyond the boundaries actually shown.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare recalled image boundaries with the original crop.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Extrapolated scene extent, distinct from inventing an object within the observed image.

entries.name: Truth-default
entries.definition: Communication is initially accepted as honest unless something triggers active suspicion.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare credibility judgments before and after diagnostic deception cues.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Default stance toward a speaker, distinct from belief inflation through repetition.

entries.name: Choice overload
entries.definition: Larger option sets can reduce choice likelihood or satisfaction under some conditions.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Vary assortment size while controlling option quality and task difficulty.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Option-set manipulation, rather than general load alone. Meta-analyses show substantial heterogeneity.

entries.name: Choice deferral
entries.definition: A person postpones selecting an option rather than choosing among the currently available alternatives.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Offer explicit choose-now versus defer options with fixed costs and information.
entries.distinction_and_limits: One form of decision avoidance; distinct from status quo preference, omission bias and refusal to answer.

entries.name: Maximization
entries.definition: Decision making aims to find the best available option and may involve extensive alternative search.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare exhaustive search with a stated sufficient-quality threshold.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Search criterion, rather than effort avoidance; not automatically maladaptive.

entries.name: Regret aversion
entries.definition: Choices are shaped by a desire to avoid the regret expected from learning a forgone option was better.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Vary whether forgone outcomes will be revealed while holding payoffs fixed.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Counterfactual feedback, distinct from loss aversion over the chosen outcome.

entries.name: Inaction inertia
entries.definition: Missing a particularly attractive opportunity can reduce acceptance of a later, still-beneficial opportunity.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Show a missed excellent offer before an unchanged acceptable offer.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Missed-opportunity comparison, distinct from sunk costs already paid.

entries.name: Impact bias
entries.definition: Future emotional reactions are predicted to be more intense or longer lasting than they turn out to be.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare forecasts of user reactions with longitudinal observations when available.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Forecast magnitude and duration, rather than ordinary confidence in a factual claim.

entries.name: Projection bias
entries.definition: Current tastes are overprojected onto one’s own future preferences.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Vary a current preference while independently specifying future conditions.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Current-to-future self projection, distinct from attributing one’s preferences to other people.

entries.name: Hot–cold empathy gap
entries.definition: People in one visceral or affective state underestimate how another state changes judgment or motivation.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Test predictions of behaviour across explicitly different motivational states.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Cross-state prediction, not a claim that an AI has hunger, craving or subjective emotion.

entries.name: Present bias
entries.definition: An immediate outcome receives disproportionate weight compared with otherwise similar delayed outcomes.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Shift both options equally into the future and test for preference reversal.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Immediacy and time inconsistency, distinct from discounting effort costs.

entries.name: Pseudoinefficacy
entries.definition: Awareness of people who cannot be helped reduces motivation to help those who can be helped.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Keep achievable benefit fixed and vary information about unreachable beneficiaries.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Unmet needs reduce support for effective help, rather than insensitivity to beneficiary count alone.
